policy.interpretation: Primary estimates assume P=1/Q=9; all games contribute to the combined fit, with whole-position out-of-fold predictions.

method.ridgeScale: mean game-weighted loss; penalty on standardized slopes
method.weighting: each sampled game has unit total weight
method.normalizationThreshold: Conservative reporting policy, not a confidence guarantee or a reason to generate more games automatically.
method.regularizationCaveat: Ridge produces finite exploratory slopes even for some separated outcomes; absence of a perfect-classification flag does not exclude quasi-separation.
method.interpretation: Exploratory outcome-predictive coefficients conditional on this selected dataset and playing policy; not intrinsic or causal piece values.
method.anchorConstraint: beta_queen = 9 * beta_pawn with positive fitted score conversion
method.anchorPenalty: Both original pawn and queen standardized slopes retain their ridge penalties.
method.groupingCaveat: Different selected positions may share opening ancestry.

bootstrap.interpretation: Conditional whole-position percentile ranges; every cohort shares identical block multiplicities, including zero-sample groups.

normalized.interpretation: Conditional fitted ratios under assumed pawn=1 and queen=9. Fixed anchors are assumptions, not measured values or uncertainty bounds.

differences.interpretation: Paired refits use identical whole-position resample multiplicities. The ±0.5 guide is practical conditional agreement, not universal statistical equivalence.

predictions.interpretation: Predictions use only other position blocks. Matchup ranges resample complete color pairs within whole blocks; error ranges condition on the fitted out-of-fold predictions and do not refit training models.

method.bootstrapUniverse: All completed-game position groups, including groups with no eligible samples in a cohort.
method.predictionTarget: Starting-position expected White score, converted to design A perspective by color.
method.matchedOpponentContext: Cohort differences do not isolate a causal method effect.
